First, we write the integral as

$$
{\int }_{1}^{e}{log}_{4}⁡(x)\text{d}x={\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}{\int }_{1}^{e}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\cdot 1\cdot \text{d}x.
$$

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=1\, & ⟹\,v=x\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}{log}_{4}⁡(x)\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}{\int }_{1}^{e}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}{\int }_{1}^{e}u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}[uv{|}_{1}^{e}-{\int }_{1}^{e}v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}[\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)(x){|}_{1}^{e}-{\int }_{1}^{e}x(\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}[e\operatorname{ln}⁡(e)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(1)-{\int }_{1}^{e}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}[e-x{|}_{1}^{e}\,] \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}(e-e+1) \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}.\end{aligned}
$$
